judgments.yea_description: Voted for House Bill 1062, which extended aggravated assault to threats with a realistic fake weapon. Aggravated assault already covered menacing someone with a deadly weapon so as to put them in fear of serious harm. The act adds a physical object that realistically simulates a deadly weapon, so a convincing replica counts. The rest of the section is reorganized and two subsections repealed years ago are removed, without changing what they cover. The South Dakota House vote was 44-22. The Governor signed it on March 09, 2026.

judgments.yea_description: Voted for House Bill 1064, which allowed direct sales of uninspected meat once federal law permits them. A custom exempt plant slaughters animals for their owner and is not subject to the full inspection that meat sold at retail requires. The act lets a producer sell meat from cattle, sheep, swine or goats slaughtered at such a plant straight to the person eating it. The animal must have been raised by that producer for at least ninety days and slaughtered and processed in South Dakota; the seller must hand it over in person at their home, a farmers market, a roadside stand or a similar temporary venue; and the package must be labeled as uninspected and not for resale. None of this takes effect until the Attorney General certifies that federal law, by statute or a final court ruling, allows such sales. The South Dakota House vote was 48-18. The Governor signed it on February 17, 2026.

judgments.yea_description: Voted for House Bill 1066, which broadened when a contractor who misuses a customer's money commits theft. The old law reached a contractor who knowingly used more than $500 of a payment for something other than the job, and only while bills for that job were unpaid. The act instead covers any contractor, subcontractor or supplier entrusted with another person's property who, intending to defraud, uses it for anything other than the labor, skill or materials it was given for. Penalties follow the general theft scale, so they rise with the amount. The South Dakota House vote was 46-19. The Governor signed it on March 30, 2026.

judgments.yea_description: Voted for House Bill 1084, which hid the home details of judges and police from the public voter file. Only judges' home addresses used to be withheld from the voter registration file. The act withholds the home address, home or personal phone number and personal email of current and retired state and federal judges and of law enforcement officers, from both the current file and the state's five-year archive. The city and county where the person lives stays public. The courts and the Division of Criminal Investigation must send the Secretary of State the lists of who is covered. The South Dakota House vote was 53-14. The Governor signed it on March 09, 2026.

judgments.yea_description: Voted for House Bill 1130, which let a school district pay its property insurance premiums from its capital outlay fund. The capital outlay fund is raised by its own property tax levy and pays for land, buildings, grounds and equipment. It could already cover up to fifteen percent of a student transportation contract or mileage reimbursement, textbooks, instructional software and warranties on capital assets. The act rewrites that list as numbered items and adds one new use: premiums on a property insurance policy the district holds. The South Dakota House vote was 41-25. The Governor signed it on March 04, 2026.

judgments.yea_description: Voted for House Bill 1244, which paid for a program keeping at-risk students on track to graduate. The act appropriates $500,000 to the Department of Education for a grant to a nonprofit in the state that supports school districts and accredited nonpublic schools running Jobs for America's Graduates, a program for students at risk of not finishing school. The grant may only match private donations, match federal education or career readiness grants, or support wider joint efforts. The act also repeals the special donations fund. The South Dakota House vote was 51-14. The Governor signed it on March 30, 2026.

judgments.yea_description: Voted for Senate Bill 106, which raised the money held back for costly special education cases. Each year the Department of Education holds back part of the special education appropriation to cover extraordinary costs of teaching a child with disabilities. That set-aside had been $4 million a year since 2014. The act raises it to $5 million from July 1, 2026. Unspent money still carries over, and the total held in reserve may not exceed $5.5 million. An oversight board still reviews districts' requests and the secretary still approves them. The South Dakota House vote was 54-15. The Governor signed it on March 30, 2026.

judgments.yea_description: Voted for Senate Bill 76, which let the housing infrastructure fund lend money for airports. The South Dakota housing infrastructure fund exists to pay for public works that support housing projects. The act lets the housing authority lend from that fund for airport infrastructure as well, and requires it to write rules setting how such a loan is applied for, approved and paid out. The South Dakota House vote was 43-24. The Governor signed it on March 30, 2026.
